version.changelog: Full pipeline rewrite: Bear #share → JSON Canvas → BlueBubbles with state tracking, canvas-schema reference, improved scripts

llm.summary: The skill’s stated Bear-to-canvas-to-iMessage workflow is mostly disclosed, but it handles private note content with unsafe command patterns and weak controls around external sharing.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads Bear note bodies using a local grizzly token and sends up to 280 characters externally via a configured messaging target, but it lacks strong recipient verification, redaction, or per-send confirmation guidance.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No hidden installer, dependency fetch, tool replacement, or automatic startup mechanism was found in the artifact; scheduling is described as a user-configured cron/OpenClaw cron option.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The documented pipeline and polling script interpolate note data, state paths, and BEAR_SHARE_TARGET into inline Python source, creating a realistic local code-execution risk if note content or configuration is hostile.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It persists processed note IDs under the user home directory by default and encourages recurring polling; this is disclosed, but the state handling is fragile and a filter bug can repeatedly re-emit already processed notes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md header and workflow clearly describe polling Bear notes tagged #share, writing note excerpts into a JSON Canvas file, and preparing BlueBubbles/iMessage previews, so the core behavior is coherent with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing. It is intended to move tagged Bear note content into a canvas and prepare iMessage previews, so only use it with notes and recipients you trust. The current scripts should be fixed before scheduled use: pass JSON and configuration as data instead of inline Python source, validate the message target, add explicit confirmation or redaction for note previews, and correct the processed-note filter.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The claimed mismatch is not supported by the artifact: canvas writing and preview distribution are explicitly stated in the description and workflow.
[LP3] expected: Local canvas and state-file writes are expected for this workflow and documented, though explicit permission scoping and backup/dry-run guidance are weak.
[SQP-2] expected: Outbound iMessage preview sharing is disclosed, but the artifact does not adequately warn that Bear note excerpts may contain sensitive information or verify the target before sending.
[SSD-3] expected: Sharing note previews is part of the stated purpose, but the one-shot and scheduled workflow can forward snippets without an interactive review step.
[RA2] expected: The state file and optional cron scheduling are disclosed rather than hidden persistence, so this is a control and scoping concern, not evidence of a backdoor.
[SDI-1] expected: Reading note bodies and writing excerpts into a canvas are disclosed by SKILL.md, but full note content is still handled and emitted by the polling step before truncation downstream.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Use of the grizzly token is disclosed, but the --enable-callback flag is not explained and broadens the access surface beyond simple local polling.
[SDI-4] expected: The implementation docstring and manifest both describe canvas updates, so the alleged intent divergence is not supported.
[T09] unexpected: I independently confirmed inline python3 -c blocks embed RAW note JSON, STATE_FILE, and BEAR_SHARE_TARGET as program text, making code injection a material security concern.
[T09] unexpected: I independently confirmed the processed-note filter treats any non-empty id as truthy, which can cause already processed notes to be output again and repeatedly previewed.
